# Retail Support

`customer_support.model.b2c.retail` · vertical · parent `customer_support.model.b2c`

> Supporting consumers of an omnichannel retailer — stores, online, click-and-collect, and every combination customers invent between them. This vertical shares most of its queue with consumer ecommerce; what genuinely differs is that the contact centre is not where the resolution happens. A store is both a channel and a resolution locus that support does not manage. The customer can walk in, and whatever we told them online will be tested at a till by a colleague who never saw the ticket, has different information, and has their own opinion about the policy. A very large share of "resolved" here means "told the customer to go to the store", which is an out-of-system handoff with no acknowledgement, no clock and no closure — and it is the single largest source of repeat contact in this vertical. Inventory truth is per-location and stale. The stock figure the customer saw, the one the agent sees and the one on the shelf are three different numbers, and none of them is authoritative enough to promise on. The knowledge layer carries the whole operation because the people do not persist. Peak is staffed by temporary agents ramped in days, so the macro library and the article set are effectively the standard of service, and a policy change that does not reach them has not happened. The error carried in from pure-play ecommerce is assuming the queue owns the outcome. The error carried in from B2B is investing in individual agent expertise: here the durable asset is the content, because the agent will be gone in eleven weeks.


## Characteristics

|  |  |
|---|---|
| requester | a shopper who may have bought in store, online or both, and who does not distinguish between the two even when our systems do |
| typical_resolution_hours | 5 |
| volume_shape | high volume with pronounced trading-calendar peaks, promotional and pricing-error spikes, and a post-holiday returns and gift-card wave |
| staffing_model | pooled contact centre plus store colleagues who resolve without ever touching the queue, heavy seasonal temporary staffing |
| coverage | aligned to trading hours across regions, seven days, extended through peak |
| automation_level | high on order and returns intents, low on anything involving a specific store's stock or a colleague's decision |
| notes | The out-of-system resolution rate — contacts closed by sending the customer to a store — is the metric this vertical most needs and least often has. Without it, repeat contact looks like a customer problem rather than a handoff problem.  |

## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.ticket`

Requires `channel`, `resolution_type`


> Resolution type needs a value for "handed to a store", explicitly and separately from resolved. Collapsing the two is what makes the repeat contact three days later look like a new problem, and it is why the same customer is asked to explain themselves twice.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.knowledge_article`

Requires `audience`, `locale`, `last_verified_at`


> Audience separates the customer-facing policy page from the agent-facing macro, and they drift apart constantly: a promotion changes, the public page is updated, the macro is not, and for two weeks the contact centre contradicts the website in writing.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.customer_sentiment`

Requires `public_exposure`, `channel_switch`


> Channel switching is the escalation ladder here — chat, then phone, then walking into a store, then a review. Each step widens the audience and lowers the chance of a clean resolution, so a switch is worth reading as a warning rather than as a preference.
